text: Advance care planning includes clarifying values, choosing a surrogate, discussing future medical care and documenting preferences; paperwork is one part of the process. (medium confidence)

text: Advance care planning is a continuing discussion of future care needs, wishes and preferences, including decisions for a time when a person may be unable to decide independently. (high confidence)

text: Individual readiness and timing matter: interview findings support regularly revisiting information preferences, while the PD_Pal contextual analysis found both resistance when discussion felt premature and cognitive limitations that could obstruct later participation. (medium confidence)

text: PD_Pal’s authors identify fragmented electronic-record documentation and limited visibility as possible reasons recorded preferences may be missed; documentation alone may not capture the quality or process of ACP discussions. (low confidence)

text: The 2020 randomized trial enrolled 210 people with PD or related disorders with moderate-to-high palliative needs; at 6 months the palliative-care group had better quality of life (treatment effect 1.87; 95% CI 0.47–3.27). Its mixed diagnostic population and selected needs limit extrapolation to all PD patients. (low confidence)

text: The 2020 trial found improved advance-directive completion among secondary outcomes, but its lack of demographic diversity and conduct at experienced academic centers limit generalizability. (low confidence)

text: Lum and colleagues recommend starting ACP discussions early because later communication and cognitive difficulties can reduce participation; they also recommend checking readiness, knowledge and information needs rather than assuming everyone wants the same discussion. (low confidence)

text: In that 2020 trial, among participants without an advance directive at baseline, six-month completion was 53% with palliative care versus 26% with standard care; the health-care-proxy completion comparison was not significant. (low confidence)

text: In the 2021 qualitative interview study of 20 patients, most wanted ACP discussion with a clinician and the majority preferred clinician initiation early in the disease; preferred information timing varied. These are participant perspectives rather than evidence that everyone wants immediate detailed end-of-life planning. (low confidence)

text: Palliative care addresses symptoms, psychosocial concerns and future planning; NICE recommends considering referral at any stage of PD, so it need not wait until the terminal phase. (high confidence)
keywords: Palliative and advance care planning in PD

text: NICE’s 2017 PD recommendations advise oral and written information about progression, future treatment options and end-of-life issues, with the discussion recorded; named UK planning mechanisms include ADRT, DNACPR and Lasting Power of Attorney. These are UK guideline examples, not universal legal instruments. (low confidence)

text: In the 2026 PD_Pal trial, 189 participants with advanced parkinsonism were randomized to a six-month nurse-led ACP and care-coordination intervention or usual care; documented end-of-life preferences did not differ significantly at six months (P=0.77). This trial does not establish that structured ACP universally improves documentation. (low confidence)

text: Benefits in one palliative-care trial should not be generalized to every ACP intervention: the 2020 intervention improved advance-directive completion, whereas PD_Pal in 2026 did not improve its primary documentation endpoint. They tested different interventions and populations. (medium confidence)

text: The 2020 trial did not demonstrate a significant between-group reduction in healthcare use; the authors cautioned that relevant events were few. Reduced hospitalization should not be presented as an established result of that trial. (low confidence)
